## 4. The independent transport mechanism also exposed a precise global obstruction

I also developed the row construction through unary maps

\[
T_{b,c}(x)=m(x,b,c).
\]

The Maltsev identities require

\[
T_{b,b}=\operatorname{id},
\qquad
T_{b,c}(b)=c.
\]

For reflexive relations, preservation further requires these maps to be endomorphisms. Acquiring all such unary maps separately looks substantially easier than acquiring a full ternary operation. It is insufficient.

Take

\[
D=\{0,1,2\},
\qquad
E=\{00,11,12,21,22\}.
\]

Define

\[
T_{b,c}(x)=
\begin{cases}
x,&b=c,\\
c,&b\ne c.
\end{cases}
\]

Every map preserves \(E\), and both displayed identity requirements hold. The assembled operation satisfies the Maltsev identities.

Yet on the three \(E\)-rows

\[
(0,0),\qquad(1,1),\qquad(1,2),
\]

its output is

\[
(0,2)\notin E.
\]

The necessary compatibility uses **different parameter pairs in different coordinates**. Separate unary preservation checks do not enforce it.

### Making every transport invertible would exclude valid Maltsev inputs

There is a useful general theorem here.

> **If a Maltsev polymorphism has every map \(x\mapsto m(x,b,c)\) bijective, then every nonempty pp-definable relation has equally sized nonempty fibres under every coordinate projection.**

To prove it, let \(R\) be such a relation and choose \(s,t\in R\). The coordinatewise map

\[
T(x)=m(x,s,t)
\]

preserves \(R\) and is injective, hence bijective because \(R\) is finite. Its induced map on any projected relation is also bijective, taking the projection of \(s\) to that of \(t\). It therefore maps the entire fibre above one projection bijectively onto the other.

But \(E\) above has first-coordinate fibres of sizes

\[
1,\;2,\;2.
\]

So no sufficient operation for this valid input can have every transport invertible.

A Maltsev witness for \(E\) is easy to exhibit. Let \(q(0)=0\), \(q(1)=q(2)=1\), and set

\[
m(x,y,z)=
\begin{cases}
z,&x=y,\\
z,&q(x)=q(y)\ne q(z),\\
x,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]

The identities hold, and the output block depends only on the three input blocks, proving preservation.

This rules out completing the general transport mechanism by silently imposing a group of bijections. General Maltsev compatibility must allow collapse and unequal fibres.

The proof note also contains a positive calibration: a complete Latin three-sort table can be normalize

## 5. Exact resource status

The operation table is small enough to store, and verification is polynomial.

For a candidate \(m\), deterministic verification uses, up to encoding factors,

\[
O\!\left(
\left[d^2+\sum_j k_jt_j^3\right]\log(2+N)
\right)
\]

coordinate operations.

The identities fix \(2d^2-d\) table positions, leaving

\[
d^3-2d^2+d=d(d-1)^2
\]

positions. Exhaustively filling those positions yields a correct acquisition procedure with bound

\[
\boxed{
d^{\,d(d-1)^2}\operatorname{poly}(N).
}
\]

After acquisition, polynomial transfer is available. Lagerkvist’s October 2026 Theorem 4.7 gives the supplied-operation bound

\[
O\!\left(d^5v^2\|I\|\right),
\]

where \(v\) is the number of variables and the constraint data are explicitly represented. Its procedures evaluate the operation, so this bound cannot be charged as the acquisition step. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="4"}

The end-to-end bound actually justified here therefore still has exponential preprocessing. I have not established fixed polynomials \(P,Q\) giving

\[
P(N)+\sum_j Q(N,|I_j|).
\]

What this attempt adds is a checked rejection of a purported complete solution at its exact global operation, together with an independently developed row formulation and precise tests of its proposed simplifications. **The remaining unproved step is acquiring compatible actual outputs across all row maps in polynomial time.** Neither a signed linear solution, separately correct transports, exact boundary pairs, nor a supplied compact-representation mechanism earns that step.
